title: India Biennale 2026 opens in Delhi on 4 December, with Purana Qila as its main venue
dek: The Ministry of Culture's second biennale of art, architecture and design runs for 108 days, to 21 March 2027, across Delhi's monuments, museums and galleries, on the Upanishadic theme Tat Tvam Asi.
body: The India Biennale 2026, organised by the Ministry of Culture, will run in Delhi from 4 December 2026 to 21 March 2027, a span of 108 days. The ministry's biennale website describes it as the second edition. A PTI report of 31 October says it follows the first India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale, held in 2023, and India's pavilion at the 61st Venice Art Biennale in 2026.

The theme is Tat Tvam Asi, the Upanishadic phrase usually rendered 'You are that'. The website sets out four threads, Reflection, Rejuvenation, Renewal and Resilience, with the five senses as a common lens, and says work in any medium is welcome, from handmade to digital.

Purana Qila is the main venue. According to PTI, the programme also reaches the Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Safdarjung Tomb, Lodhi Garden, Mehrauli, the National Gallery of Modern Art, the National Museum and the Lalit Kala Akademi. On 16 November the website listed 45 exhibitions, presented by foundations, galleries, design studios, a university, museums, embassies and foreign cultural institutes.

Among the listed shows with a heritage subject are an 18th-century Mahabharata scroll presented by DAG and a Bihar Museum exhibition on Chhath Puja and Pind Daan, both at Purana Qila; a Ganesh Shivaswamy Foundation show on Raja Ravi Varma's legacy through photography at the National Gallery of Modern Art; and a Cultural Resource Conservation Initiative project on Mehrauli's water history, which PTI says spans the Mehrauli Archaeological Park. A Student Biennale is also planned at Purana Qila.

Entry to the participating venues is by a single Biennale Pass in place of separate tickets. PTI gives the prices as Rs 100 for one day, Rs 200 for three days, Rs 400 for a week, Rs 3,000 for the season and Rs 10,000 for a premium pass with parking and guided walkthroughs. The calendar of talks, walks and performances was still marked 'coming soon' on the website on 16 November.
